subject: Optimize toolkit: packaging, quantization guidance + commitment counteroffer
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.r@finopsco.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@finopsco.com, Tom Li <tom.li@finopsco.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit inquiry - batching/caching/quantization

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Optimize suggestions looked promising. Before we take internal procurement forward we need: a clean view of packaging (what's in "Optimize Starter" vs "Pro"), realistic token-cost reduction ranges for batching + prefix caching, and firm guidance on quantization options for our LLM stacks.

Our current monthly usage estimate is ~150M tokens (chat + embeddings) with spiky peaks. We care about predictable unit economics more than aggressive lowest price. Procurement also asked for: 12-month committed pricing, any reserved capacity add-ons, and compliance notes (SOC 2, EU data region).

Can you send a short proposal with: 1) recommended package for our workload, 2) expected % savings (batching + caching + quantization) at our scale, 3) discount tiers for a 12-mo commit, and 4) next steps / timeline (procurement path).

If helpful, Tom (cc'd) will be the procurement lead.

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
FinOpsCo

--
Attachment: none
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.r@finopsco.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@finopsco.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit inquiry - packaging and initial pricing proposal

Elena —

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a concise proposal and a quantization savings workbook that walks through a few example model flavors. High level summary below:

Recommendation: Optimize Pro (includes adaptive batching, prefix/KV caching, cost-savings rules engine, & dedicated recommendations from our Optimize team). For your usage profile (~150M tokens/month with spikes) Pro hits the balance of latency SLOs + meaningful unit-cost reduction.

Estimated savings (typical ranges, conservative):
- Batching improvements (continuous batching with latency-aware windows): 8–16% token cost reduction depending on peak distribution
- Prefix/KV caching (chat + repeat prompts): 6–12% on top of batching for conversational flows with repeated context
- Quantization (per-model basis; recommended path: 8-bit Q5 -> mixed-int8 inference): 18–28% reduction in token compute costs for compatible models
- Combined (conservative stacked estimate): 28–40% unit-cost reduction; best-case 45%+ after model-specific tuning

Packaging & pricing (starter list):
- Optimize Starter: basic recommendations, monthly reports, up to 50M tokens; $1,200/mo
- Optimize Pro: full toolkit + routing policies + 24/7 support for inference ops; recommended for you; $7,500/mo base + usage
- Enterprise: dedicated Optimize engineers, advanced eval integration, custom quantization profiles; custom pricing

Discount guidance for 12-month commit (list-price anchors):
- 12-mo, $100k+ ARR: 12% standard kickback
- 12-mo, $250k+ ARR: 16%
- 12-mo, $500k+ ARR: 20% + custom quantization tuning batch

Procurement notes: SOC 2: Type II in the compliance pack (we'll share the evidence). EU data region: we can route inference to eu-west by default for your tenant.

Attachments: Optimize_Pricing_Overview.pdf (pricing tiers and short SOW), Quantization_Savings_Sheet.xlsx (per-model worked examples).

Next steps: 1) If you agree, we can draft an MOU and a mutual action plan; 2) Procurement review (Tom); 3) Finalize 12-mo commitment and counters.

Would you be available for a short 30-min call on Monday to run through the workbook? I can bring Ben (solutions) and Monica (CS).

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.inference
+1 415-555-0192

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit inquiry - packaging and initial pricing proposal

Lauren —

Thanks for the detailed breakdown, that helps a lot. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering:
1) Procurement wants a firm commitment-level price per token (post-discount) for the 12-mo, 150M token estimate and for an optional reserved GPU add-on (we'd like a committed burst pool).
2) Engineering asked for explicit model compatibility notes for our internal LLaMA-derivative stack — can you confirm which quantization modes you support today and whether mixed-int8 requires a different runtime?
3) Can you confirm the SLA and what happens if caching/batching causes a QoS regression for tail latency?

If you can send a short redlineable MOU and an example cost table (monthly breakdown) we can loop procurement and legal. Tom can take a call Monday afternoon.

Regards,
Elena
